faq_heading: Princeton lots and land: your questions answered

faq.q: Can I build a house and a suite on a Princeton lot?
faq.a: Under BC’s 2023 small-scale multi-unit housing law, every municipality must allow a secondary suite or a detached accessory dwelling on most single-family lots. Check the zone with the Town of Princeton (or the Regional District for rural land) first.

faq.q: Who issues building permits in Princeton?
faq.a: The Town of Princeton inside town limits, and the Regional District of Okanagan-Similkameen for rural Electoral Area H.

faq.q: Are Princeton lots in a floodplain?
faq.a: Some near the Tulameen and Similkameen rivers are. Ask the Town or the Regional District about the specific lot before you buy.

faq.q: Can I book a private showing with Jared?
faq.a: Yes. Jared Gibbons, REALTOR® with Royal LePage Little Oak Realty, books private showings across the Fraser Valley and Metro Vancouver. Call or text 604-928-1361, or use the contact form on this site.

parts.t: Land in Princeton runs from serviced town lots to bare rural parcels in the valley. This search lists vacant lots and land for sale in and around Princeton. Jared has sold in Princeton:
a three-bedroom house on Similkameen Avenue
a house and shop on two RM3-zoned lots on Angela Avenue

items.t: Town lots:
zoned by the Town of Princeton and served by Town water and sewer. The Official Community Plan Bylaw No. 1044, 2023 sets where the town plans to grow to 2042.
Rural land:
zoned by the Regional District under Electoral Area H Zoning Bylaw No. 3065, 2024, and usually needing a well and septic.
Suites:

under the Province’s 2023 small-scale multi-unit housing law, every BC municipality must allow a secondary suite or a detached accessory dwelling on most single-family lots. The three-to-four-unit rule applies only in municipalities of more than 5,000 people, and Princeton has under 3,000.

blocks.text: Before you buy a lot in Princeton

items.t: Floodplain:
ask the Town or the Regional District whether the lot is in a floodplain; the 2021 flood reached both river valleys.
Services:
for a town lot, ask the Town what it costs to connect water and sewer and whether development cost charges apply. For rural land, price a well and septic system first.
What you can build:
read the zone for height, setbacks and lot coverage, and whether a suite or carriage house is allowed.
Building permits:
the Town issues permits in town; the Regional District issues them in Area H.
